subproblems.title: Allard scale at a point of density one (Simon 7.1, proof, first sentence)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an open subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold n l U) with weight mu = mu_V, H : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l), and p a real number with p > n, such that H is locally in L^p(mu) on U (integral over K of |H|^p dmu < infinity for every compact K contained in U). Let xi be in U with Theta^n(mu, xi) = 1, i.e. mu(B_r(xi)) / (omega_n r^n) -> 1 as r decreases to 0 (closed balls, quotient in [0, infinity]), and let delta > 0. Then xi is in spt V = U cap spt mu, and there is r > 0 with B_r(xi) contained in U, mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n and (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta (both inequalities in [0, infinity], the second being V.scaledLpNorm H p xi r <= delta).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p : ℝ) (ξ : Amb n ℓ) (δ : ℝ), IsOpen U → (n : ℝ) < p → V.LocallyLp H p → ξ ∈ U → V.HasDensity ξ 1 → 0 < δ → ξ ∈ V.support ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ closedBall ξ r ⊆ U ∧ V.weight (closedBall ξ r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + δ) * (unitBallVolume n * r ^ n)) ∧ V.scaledLpNorm H p ξ r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: Submission.density_one_allard_scale (DAG node root.density_one_regularity-a1.allard_scale-a1, status accepted, reviewed candidate commit 556f326ab6126af50cb093c48702a0aefff24952; math-wiki page submission-density-one-allard-scale.md). The frozen Lean type is byte-identical to that node's, so the controller maps this child to the existing accepted node and no new proof work is created. The proof below is that node's independently approved proof. In the present parent it supplies steps 3-4 (choice of the scale rho and xi in spt V), applied with delta := delta_0.

Source: Simon, Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 7.1, first sentence (p. 127): 'Since lim_{rho->0} (rho^(p-n) int_{B_rho(xi)} |H|^p dmu_V)^(1/p) = 0 and lim_{rho->0} (omega_n rho^n)^(-1) mu_V(B_rho(xi)) = 1, we can choose rho > 0 such that the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2 hold'. Notation: mu = V.weight, omega_n = unitBallVolume n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2+1) > 0, balls B_r closed, all masses and integrals of nonnegative functions in [0, infinity].

1. Put m(r) := mu(B_r(xi)), v(r) := omega_n r^n in (0, infinity) for r > 0, and Q(r) := m(r)/v(r) in [0, infinity]. The hypothesis V.HasDensity xi 1 says exactly Q(r) -> 1 as r -> 0+.

2. xi is in spt mu. Let N be any neighbourhood of xi and choose e > 0 with B_e(xi) contained in N. Since Q(r) -> 1 > 0, the set of r in (0, e) with Q(r) > 0 is nonempty; for such r, m(r) > 0 (if m(r) = 0 then Q(r) = 0). Hence mu(N) >= m(r) > 0. As N was arbitrary, xi is in the support of mu, and since xi is in U, xi is in spt V = U cap spt mu.

3. Since U is open, choose r_0 > 0 with B_{r_0}(xi) contained in U. K := B_{r_0}(xi) is compact (closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional space) and contained in U, so A := integral_K |H|^p dmu < infinity by the local L^p hypothesis.

4. Mass bound for small r. Since Q(r) -> 1 < 1 + delta, there is r_1 in (0, r_0] such that Q(r) < 1 + delta for all r in (0, r_1). For such r, because v(r) is finite and positive, m(r) = Q(r) v(r) <= (1 + delta) v(r) = (1 + delta) omega_n r^n.

5. L^p bound for small r. For 0 < r <= r_0 we have B_r(xi) contained in K, so integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu <= A, and therefore S(r) := (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= (r^(p-n) A)^(1/p), using that t -> t^(1/p) is nondecreasing on [0, infinity] (p > n >= 0, so 1/p > 0). As r -> 0+, r^(p-n) -> 0 because p - n > 0; since A < infinity, r^(p-n) A -> 0 in [0, infinity), and since t -> t^(1/p) is continuous at 0 with 0^(1/p) = 0, (r^(p-n) A)^(1/p) -> 0. As delta > 0, there is r_2 in (0, r_0] with S(r) <= delta for all r in (0, r_2).

6. Let r := min(r_1, r_2)/2 > 0. Then r <= r_0, so B_r(xi) is contained in B_{r_0}(xi), which is contained in U; r < r_1 gives mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n by step 4, and r < r_2 gives (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta by step 5. Together with step 2 this proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: Positive density at xi forces mu(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N, so xi is in spt V
Fix a compact ball B_{r_0}(xi) in U; its |H|^p-integral A is finite
Mass ratio tends to 1 < 1 + delta, so the mass bound holds for small r
Scaled L^p norm is at most (r^(p-n) A)^(1/p), which tends to 0 since p > n
Take r below both thresholds and below r_0

subproblems.title: Translation of a rectifiable varifold and transfer of the hypotheses 5.1 to the origin
subproblems.statement: Let U be any subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure) with weight mu, xi in R^(n+l), and tau(x) := x - xi. Then there is a rectifiable n-varifold V' in tau(U) with carrier tau(M), multiplicity theta'(x) = theta(x + xi) for all x, weight mu_{V'} = tau_# mu (Measure.map), and spt V' = tau(spt V), such that: (i) if V has generalized mean curvature H in U then V' has generalized mean curvature H' := H(. + xi) in tau(U); (ii) for all H and reals p, delta, r: if V has generalized mean curvature H in U, theta >= 1 mu-a.e., xi is in spt V, r > 0, B_r(xi) is contained in U, mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n and (r^(p-n) int_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta, then V' satisfies the hypotheses 5.1 at the origin: V'.AllardHypotheses H' p delta r.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ), ∃ V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ ((fun x => x - ξ) '' U), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.carrier ∧ (∀ x, V'.mult x = V.mult (x + ξ)) ∧ V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - ξ) ∧ V'.support = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.support ∧ (∀ H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ, V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → V'.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun x => H (x + ξ))) ∧ ∀ (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p δ r : ℝ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, 1 ≤ V.mult x) → ξ ∈ V.support → 0 < r → closedBall ξ r ⊆ U → V.weight (closedBall ξ r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + δ) * (unitBallVolume n * r ^ n)) → V.scaledLpNorm H p ξ r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ → V'.AllardHypotheses (fun x => H (x + ξ)) p δ r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: Submission.exists_translated_varifold_allardHypotheses (DAG node root.density_one_regularity-a1.translate_varifold-a1, status accepted, reviewed candidate commit e8ad21ac2377accf942ccc877ba9e134580373cd; math-wiki page submission-exists-translated-varifold-allardhypotheses.md). The frozen Lean type is byte-identical to that node's, so the controller maps this child to the existing accepted node and no new proof work is created. The proof below is that node's independently approved proof. In the present parent it supplies steps 2 and 5: the translate V' (the role of dohr_translate_varifold) and the seven parts of AllardHypotheses for V' at (p, delta, rho).

Source: the translation step 'after applying the appropriate translation' of Simon's proof of 7.1 (p. 127), proved in detail from the contract definitions. Notation: H^n = muHE[n]; mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta); tau(x) = x - xi with inverse tau^{-1}(x) = x + xi; for a set A, tau(A) = {a - xi : a in A} = (tau^{-1})^{-1}(A).

1. tau is a bijective isometry of R^(n+l), hence a homeomorphism and a measurable equivalence (Borel sets to Borel sets, both ways). Hausdorff measures, and hence H^n = muHE[n], are invariant under isometries: H^n(tau(A)) = H^n(A) for every A, tau_# H^n = H^n and (tau^{-1})_# H^n = H^n (tau is measure preserving for H^n).

2. Construction of V'. Put M' := tau(M) and theta'(x) := theta(x + xi). The structure fields hold:
(a) M' is contained in tau(U) since M is contained in U.
(b) M' = (tau^{-1})^{-1}(M) is H^n-null-measurable, because M is and preimages of null-measurable sets under the measure-preserving map tau^{-1} are null-measurable.
(c) M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M is contained in M_0 union U_j F_j(R^n) with H^n(M_0) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' is contained in tau(M_0) union U_j (tau o F_j)(R^n), H^n(tau(M_0)) = H^n(M_0) = 0, and tau o F_j is Lipschitz with the same constant.
(d) If x is in M' then x + xi is in M, so theta'(x) = theta(x + xi) > 0.
(e) H^n restricted to M' equals tau_#(H^n restricted to M) (for Borel A: tau_#(H^n|M)(A) = H^n(tau^{-1}(A) cap M) = H^n(tau(tau^{-1}(A) cap M)) = H^n(A cap M')), and theta' o tau = theta; since a function f is a.e.-measurable for tau_# nu iff f o tau is a.e.-measurable for nu (tau a measurable equivalence), theta' is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M'.
(f) If K is compact and contained in tau(U), then K' := tau^{-1}(K) = K + xi is compact and contained in U, M' cap K = tau(M cap K'), and integrability (a.e. strong measurability together with finiteness of the integral) transfers as a whole under the measure-preserving equivalence tau: theta' is H^n-integrable on tau(M cap K') iff theta' o tau = theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K', which holds by hypothesis.
So V' := v(M', theta') is a rectifiable n-varifold in tau(U), with carrier tau(M) and multiplicity theta(. + xi) by construction.

3. Weight. For Borel A: (tau_# mu)(A) = mu(tau^{-1}(A)) = int_{tau^{-1}(A)} ofReal(theta) d(H^n|M) = int_A ofReal(theta o tau^{-1}) d(tau_#(H^n|M)) = int_A ofReal(theta') d(H^n|M') = mu_{V'}(A), using the change of variables for the pushforward under the measurable equivalence tau and step 2(e). Hence mu_{V'} = tau_# mu.

4. Support. For a homeomorphism tau, spt(tau_# mu) = tau(spt mu): x is in spt(tau_# mu) iff every neighbourhood N of x has mu(tau^{-1}(N)) > 0 iff every neighbourhood of tau^{-1}(x) has positive mu-measure (tau^{-1} maps the neighbourhoods of x onto those of tau^{-1}(x)) iff tau^{-1}(x) is in spt mu. Therefore spt V' = tau(U) cap spt(mu_{V'}) = tau(U) cap tau(spt mu) = tau(U cap spt mu) = tau(spt V) (tau injective).

5. Tangent planes. For every x and every linear subspace P: P is an approximate tangent space of M' with respect to theta' at x (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7, i.e. HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' theta' x P) iff P is one of M with respect to theta at x + xi. Indeed, with eta_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y - x): eta_{x,r}(M') = {r^{-1}(m - xi - x) : m in M} = eta_{x+xi,r}(M); for y in this set theta'(x + r y) = theta((x + xi) + r y); and theta'(x) = theta(x + xi). Hence for every f in C_c and every r the integrals int_{eta_{x,r}(M')} f(y) theta'(x + r y) dH^n(y) and int_{eta_{x+xi,r}(M)} f(y) theta(x + xi + r y) dH^n(y) coincide, the limits theta'(x) int_P f dH^n and theta(x + xi) int_P f dH^n coincide, and the dimension condition is the same. Since tangentProj is defined from this predicate alone (orthogonal projection onto a chosen approximate tangent space when one exists, 0 otherwise), and the two predicates are equal as functions of P, we get tangentProj_{V'}(x) = tangentProj_V(x + xi) for all x. Either no approximate tangent space exists for either side (both values are 0), or both existence statements hold and the two chosen subspaces are choices (Classical.choose) from the same predicate, hence equal. (In Lean, rewriting the predicate inside the dependent if-then-else can fail because of the auxiliary orthogonal-projection instance proof in its body; case-split on the existence statement and prove equality of the two chosen subspaces by substituting the equal predicates.)

6. Divergence. For X in C^1 put Y := X o tau, i.e. Y(y) = X(y - xi). Then DY(y) = DX(tau y), so by step 5 div_M Y(y) = trace(DX(tau y) o tangentProj_V(y)) = trace(DX(tau y) o tangentProj_{V'}(tau y)) = div_{M'} X(tau y).

7. Proof of (i). Assume V has generalized mean curvature H in U.
(a) Local integrability: let x be in tau(U), x = tau(y) with y in U. By hypothesis there is N, a neighbourhood of y within U, with int_N |H| dmu < infinity. Then tau(N) is a neighbourhood of x within tau(U) (tau homeomorphism) and, integrability transferring as a whole under the measurable equivalence tau, H' is (tau_# mu)-integrable on tau(N) iff H' o tau = H is mu-integrable on N, since H'(tau(y)) = H(y - xi + xi) = H(y). So H' is locally integrable on tau(U) for mu_{V'} = tau_# mu.
(b) Let X be C^1 with compact support and tsupport X contained in tau(U). Then Y = X o tau is C^1, has compact support, and tsupport Y = tau^{-1}(tsupport X) is contained in U. The identity for V gives int div_M Y dmu = - int <Y, H> dmu. By the change of variables for pushforwards under the measurable equivalence tau (valid for Bochner integrals of arbitrary functions, integrable or not): int div_{M'} X dmu_{V'} = int (div_{M'} X) o tau dmu = int div_M Y dmu (step 6), and int <X, H'> dmu_{V'} = int <X(tau y), H'(tau y)> dmu(y) = int <Y, H> dmu. Hence int div_{M'} X dmu_{V'} = - int <X, H'> dmu_{V'}, i.e. V' has generalized mean curvature H' in tau(U).

8. Proof of (ii). Under the stated assumptions we check the seven parts of AllardHypotheses H' p delta r for V'.
(a) 0 < r is assumed.
(b) V' has generalized mean curvature H' in tau(U) by step 7.
(c) theta' >= 1 mu_{V'}-a.e.: for the measurable equivalence tau, a property holds (tau_# mu)-a.e. iff its composition with tau holds mu-a.e.; and 1 <= theta'(tau y) = theta(y) holds for mu-a.e. y.
(d) 0 = tau(xi) is in tau(spt V) = spt V' (step 4).
(e) B_r(0) is contained in tau(U): if |z| <= r then z + xi is in B_r(xi), which is contained in U, and z = tau(z + xi).
(f) mu_{V'}(B_r(0)) = mu(tau^{-1}(B_r(0))) = mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n, since tau^{-1}(B_r(0)) = {y : |y - xi| <= r} (closed balls are Borel).
(g) int_{B_r(0)} |H'|^p dmu_{V'} = int_{tau^{-1}(B_r(0))} |H' o tau|^p dmu = int_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu (change of variables for [0, infinity]-valued functions under a measurable equivalence; no measurability of H is needed), so (r^(p-n) int_{B_r(0)} |H'|^p dmu_{V'})^(1/p) = (r^(p-n) int_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta.
Hence V'.AllardHypotheses H' p delta r. Steps 2-8 give all asserted properties of V'.
proof_key_steps: tau(x) = x - xi is an isometric measurable equivalence preserving H^n
Define V' = v(tau(M), theta(. + xi)) and verify the structure fields
Weight of V' is the pushforward of mu; support of V' is tau(spt V)
Weighted approximate tangent spaces and hence tangentProj are translation equivariant; div_{M'} X o tau = div_M (X o tau)
Change of variables transfers the first-variation identity and local integrability
Check the seven parts of AllardHypotheses at the origin by change of variables

subproblems.title: Finite scaled C^{1,alpha} norm gives the Hoelder class C^{1,alpha}(W)
subproblems.statement: Let u : R^n -> R^l, B and W subsets of R^n with W contained in the interior of B, alpha > 0 and rho > 0. Suppose u is C^1 on B (ContDiffOn R 1 u B) and scaledC1AlphaNorm u B alpha rho = rho^{-1} sup_B |u| + sup_B |D_B u| + rho^alpha sup_{x != y in B} |D_B u(x) - D_B u(y)| / |x - y|^alpha < infinity (D_B u = derivative within B, |.| = Hilbert-Schmidt norm on linear maps, sums and suprema in [0, infinity]). Then IsHolderCkα 1 alpha u W: u is C^1 on W, there is a real Bd with ||iteratedFDeriv^i u(x)|| <= Bd for i in {0, 1} and x in W, and there is a real K with ||iteratedFDeriv^1 u(x) - iteratedFDeriv^1 u(y)|| <= K |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (B W : Set (Rn n)) (α ρ : ℝ), 0 < α → 0 < ρ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u B → W ⊆ interior B → scaledC1AlphaNorm u B α ρ ≠ ∞ → IsHolderCkα 1 α u W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: Submission.isHolderCk_one_of_scaledC1AlphaNorm_ne_top (DAG node root.density_one_regularity-a1.holder_class-a1, status accepted, reviewed candidate commit 2fa4e679ecc8f63ac77987a3b7b146f5a0d41c4b; math-wiki page submission-isholderck-one-of-scaledc1alphanorm-ne-top.md). The frozen Lean type is byte-identical to that node's, so the controller maps this child to the existing accepted node and no new proof work is created. The proof below is that node's independently approved proof. In the present parent it supplies steps 7-8 in general form, applied with B = the closed ball of radius R = gamma rho about 0 in R^n, W = the open ball of radius R about 0, alpha = 1 - n/p and the Allard scale rho.

Source: the C^{1,1-n/p} class of u obtained from the finite norm estimate of Theorem 5.2 in Simon's proof of 7.1 (p. 127), with all details.

1. Finiteness of the pieces. Write N := scaledC1AlphaNorm u B alpha rho = a S_0 + S_1 + b S_2 with a := rho^{-1} > 0, b := rho^alpha > 0, S_0 := sup_{x in B} |u(x)|, S_1 := sup_{x in B} |D_B u(x)|_HS, S_2 := sup_{x != y in B} |D_B u(x) - D_B u(y)|_HS / |x - y|^alpha, all in [0, infinity]. Since N < infinity, each summand is finite; as a and b are finite and positive, S_0, S_1, S_2 < infinity. Let s_0, s_1, s_2 >= 0 be their real values.

2. Derivatives on W. Let x be in W. Since W is contained in the interior of B, B is a neighbourhood of x; as u is C^1 on B, u is differentiable at x and D_B u(x) = Du(x) (the derivative within a neighbourhood of x is the derivative).

3. C^1 on W. W is contained in B, so u is C^1 on W (restriction of ContDiffOn to a subset).

4. Operator norm versus Hilbert-Schmidt norm. For a linear A : R^n -> R^l and v = sum_i v_i e_i: |A v| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i| <= (sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2) (sum_i |A e_i|^2)^(1/2) = |v| |A|_HS (Cauchy-Schwarz), hence ||A||_op <= |A|_HS.

5. Bounds of order 0 and 1. For x in W (contained in B): ||iteratedFDeriv^0 u(x)|| = |u(x)| <= s_0. The first iterated derivative is Du composed with the canonical linear isometry between linear maps and 1-multilinear maps, so ||iteratedFDeriv^1 u(x)|| = ||Du(x)||_op <= |Du(x)|_HS = |D_B u(x)|_HS <= s_1 (steps 2, 4). Hence Bd := max(s_0, s_1) bounds ||iteratedFDeriv^i u(x)|| for all i <= 1 and x in W.

6. Hoelder bound. Put K := s_2 and let x, y be in W. If x = y, the left side is 0 and K |x - y|^alpha = K 0^alpha = 0 because alpha > 0. If x != y, then, the canonical identification being a linear isometry, ||iteratedFDeriv^1 u(x) - iteratedFDeriv^1 u(y)|| = ||Du(x) - Du(y)||_op <= |Du(x) - Du(y)|_HS = |D_B u(x) - D_B u(y)|_HS <= s_2 |x - y|^alpha, since x != y are points of B and |x - y|^alpha > 0, so |D_B u(x) - D_B u(y)|_HS / |x - y|^alpha <= S_2.

7. Steps 3, 5, 6 are the three clauses of IsHolderCkα 1 alpha u W.
proof_key_steps: rho > 0 makes the three suprema in the scaled norm finite
At interior points the derivative within B is the derivative
Operator norm is at most the Hilbert-Schmidt norm
Order-0 and order-1 bounds and the Hoelder bound with K = sup of difference quotients
